## How it works

<h2>Explore the bridge in context</h2>
    <p>The IFC4x3 model opens on a map of San Francisco Bay. Use <strong>View → Layers</strong> to switch between street and satellite maps. Orbit to inspect the towers and deck, or select a component and open its properties from the selection count.</p>
    <p>The model declares WGS 84 / UTM zone 10N (EPSG:32610) horizontally and NAVD88 height (EPSG:5703) vertically. Its IFC map conversion places the local origin at the San Francisco tower and rotates the longitudinal axis toward the Marin tower. A horizontal grid factor fits the published span length to the projected tower separation while preserving NAVD88 elevations.</p>
    <p>The main span is 1,280.16&nbsp;m, each suspended side span is 342.90&nbsp;m, and the exterior deck width is 27.432&nbsp;m. The 2023 lidar fit uses 210 sampled stations along the roadway. The fitted tower tops are about 229.6&nbsp;m NAVD88. The cable curves, portal details, exterior piers, approach limits and other details between the survey references are reconstructed. Use the model for map placement and visual inspection.</p>

<h2>Sources and model licence</h2>
    <p>The Golden Gate Bridge IFC is original geometry released under the <a href="https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0">Apache License 2.0</a>. The survey and references have their own credits below.</p>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/inport/item/73386/full-list">2023 USGS Lidar: San Francisco, CA, NOAA InPort 73386</a> supplied the horizontal tower positions and observed deck elevations.</li>
      <li><a href="https://www.goldengate.org/bridge/history-research/statistics-data/design-construction-stats/">Golden Gate Bridge District design and construction statistics</a> supplied the published lengths, widths and cable diameter. The District’s <a href="https://www.goldengate.org/exhibits/hanging-the-roadway-deck/">deck exhibit</a> supplied the truss depth and suspender spacing.</li>
      <li><a href="https://www.loc.gov/item/38009362/">1937 chief engineer’s report, Library of Congress</a> and the District’s <a href="https://www.goldengate.org/exhibits/fort-point-arch/">Fort Point Arch exhibit</a> supplied the historical context for the visible approaches and arch.</li>
      <li><a href="https://www.goldengate.org/bridge/bridge-maintenance/painting-the-bridge/">Bridge District paint guidance</a> supplied the reference for International Orange.</li>
    </ul>
    <p>The model represents the visible exterior. Surveys, imagery and terrain may come from different dates and use different sampling resolutions.</p>
